query: What customer issues create the most support burden?

per_column.name: severity_score
per_column.rationale: Severity is a property/driver of the issue that predicts how much burden it may generate, not a constitutive part of operational burden itself. Burden is the labor/resource load; severity is an attribute of the ticket that influences it. Additionally it overlaps heavily with customer_impact_level (same 76/74/50/50 distribution), suggesting it captures the same underlying aspect.

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: A taxonomy of what the issue is about (feature_request, billing, security, etc.). This is a segmentation dimension for grouping tickets, not an aspect OF operational burden. Categorizing the issue does not decompose the burden concept into its parts (e.g., handling effort, volume, recurrence).

per_column.name: customer_impact_level
per_column.rationale: Customer-facing impact (low/medium/high/critical) is an outcome/attribute of the issue affecting the customer, not a constitutive part of the internal operational load carried by the support organization. It also mirrors severity_score's distribution, so it is largely a restatement of the same severity aspect.

judge.rationale: Operational burden is the load a support organization bears -- its constitutive facets would be aspects such as handling effort/time-to-resolve, volume/frequency, escalation/rework load, staffing/resource consumption, and recurrence. None of the added columns are parts OF this load. severity_score and customer_impact_level are external attributes/predictors of the issue (and near-duplicates of each other, hurting mutual exclusivity), while issue_category is a grouping taxonomy. The set fails the meronymy test: no column is 'an aspect of' operational burden, so exhaustiveness is 0. Note that a genuine burden facet (resolution_minutes, a handling-effort measure) already exists in the original table but was not among the added columns.
